Hi Alex — thanks for the clear numbers. Quick summary and recommended next steps below so you have something for your infra & security review.

Summary / quick read:
- Requirement: P95 <= 50 ms for user-facing flows at ~1.2k sustained QPS with burst to 1.8k. Sequence lengths moderate (220/60).
- Risk: public-hosted endpoints can meet latency targets for medium volumes but become costlier at sustained high QPS; dedicated pools give consistent tail latency and predictable unit cost. Private VPC adds compliance/isolation but increases ops lead time.

Recommendation (SLA segmentation approach):
1) Host user-facing endpoints requiring P95 <= 50 ms on Dedicated reserved capacity (GPU pool) — recommended because it gives consistent KV-cache locality and avoids noisy-neighbor latency spikes.
2) Route non-critical background tasks (P99 <= 200 ms acceptable) to Hosted API with priority routing + prefix caching — reduces committed footprint.
3) Use Smart Routing + Canary: start with a small dedicated pool (2x GPUs estimated) and route 10% traffic to dedicated for 48–72 hrs to validate tail latency; automatically fall back to Hosted if errors or cost anomalies detected.

High-level cost & perf tradeoffs:
- Dedicated: higher initial commit (reserved) but lower per-token cost at sustained QPS and better P95. Good for lowest-latency user paths.
- Hosted: best for elasticity and lower operational lift; more expensive for sustained QPS but quicker to run pilots.

Suggested pilot (2 weeks):
- Goal: validate steady-state P95 at 50 ms and measure cost/QPS delta.
- Plan: Redwood to provision dedicated pilot pool (2x A100-equivalent), enable KV prefix caching, and provide perf dashboard. We’ll run canary routing for 48–72 hrs, capture token-level latency and cost breakdowns.
- Deliverables: latency/cost dashboard, post-pilot recommendation (keep dedicated / reduce commit / fall back to hosted).

Attachments: FR-pilot-sla-bucketization-v1.pdf (pilot SLOs + routing proposal) and redwood-pilot-cost-scenarios.xlsx (cost scenarios).

Alex / Grace — quick technical notes and next actions from infra side: 

- Perf estimate: for 1.2k sustained QPS with 220/60 token profile, 2x A100-equivalent GPUs with Redwood's KV cache and batching should comfortably meet P95 ~ 30–45 ms in our benchmarks (assuming colocated region & optimized kernel path). Spikes to 1.8k will need burst capacity or autoscaling; we recommend enabling short-duration burst (additional 1–2 GPUs) or routing spike traffic to Hosted as fallback.
- Data/Compliance: SOC2 evidence (audit logs, retention, KMS integration) is available for Hosted. Private VPC adds isolation; if FastRetail's auditors require host-level separation we can provision a Private deployment but that adds ~3–4 week lead time.
- Pricing note (pilot): estimated committed cost for 2x GPUs reserved for one month: ~$25k–$33k (range depends on instance family). Equivalent hosted spend for same token volume (no commit) estimated ~$45k–$60k in our scenarios. See attached cost scenarios sheet.
